name: Wyatt
tagline: He'll tell you it's fine. The lights will tell you otherwise.
notes: Stats run 0-20 (clamped). Ending thresholds mirror Lukey: stay = romance >= 16 && friction < 8; he goes, loved = romance >= 16 (asking him to stay with friction >= 8 also gets a loving 'no'); friends = friendship >= 14 && friction < 8; 'That's up to you' gives the friends ending if friction < 8, or the polite-but-firm ending if friction >= 8. He calls you 'love' in Act 4 if romance >= 12 going in. Act 2 grudge opener if friction >= 4. 'The others' = lukey/tyler/malcolm romance >= 8 (unlocks his jealousy beats). Cross-character budget: Act 1 mentions nobody; Acts 2-4 have at most two housemate beats each (one subtle Tyler beat at most). Dan only comes once, on day 30 (inspection.json).

romance_success.title: Watt a Keeper
romance_success.text: Wyatt stayed. The wiring's up to code, the lights never flicker, and he says 'no' at least once a day just to keep his hand in. He still apologizes to the toaster. When Dan comes, he can look behind every faceplate in the house. The dehumidifier is on a very good socket.

romance_failure.title: Yeah, Nah
romance_failure.text: He loved you, and he said so first go, no 'if that's alright.' Then he said the other thing out loud too: goodbye. The wiring's perfect. The porch light still flickers twice whenever you come home. Nobody's fixing that.

friend_success.title: Current Besties
friend_success.text: Wyatt passed on in a warm, steady glow and a 'no worries' he actually meant. The fuse box is labeled properly now, in his very neat capitals. Somewhere south of Sydney, a chicken shop has a very good day for no reason anyone can explain.

friend_failure.title: No Worries (Some Worries)
friend_failure.text: Wyatt passed on politely, firmly and without a single apology. The wiring's perfect. He made sure. He left a note on the fuse box, the dehumidifier on a better socket, and the faint feeling that you should have asked him sooner.

lines: *{sfx:Spark}The fuse box pops. Sparks rain down. A slight, boyish guy with a mop of fluffy strawberry-blond hair tumbles out of it, patting out a small fire on the singed sleeve of his coat.*
*His round copper-rimmed glasses are on crooked. Below his rolled-up sleeves, his forearms aren't skin. They're braided cable: red, copper and dark grey.*
Whoa! Sorry! Hi! G'day. Sorry. Is this the doorbell? I was aiming for the doorbell.
You: This is the living room. There is no doorbell.
Right. Yep. Crossed wires. Happens heaps. I'm Wyatt. Like 'wire it.' Like, wire it [wrong].

choices.text: Hi, Wyatt. You're kind of... electric.
Are you the reason my lights flicker?
You just set my wall on fire.

lines: You: Wrong how?
Live to neutral, upside down, back to front. Everything in this house is wired wrong. I can feel it. In my teeth.
...Have I got teeth? Hang on.
*He checks.*
Yep. Teeth. Good.
*{sfx:Zap}His hair stands straight up. Literally. Static. His glasses slide down his nose, and when he shoves them back up, a tiny spark jumps off the rim.*
Electric? Me? Oh. Okay. You're making my current do a thing.
Is it hot in here? Sorry. It might be me. I'm technically a fire hazard.
Yeah. Sorry. That's me thinking. When I think hard, the bulbs go bzzt. When I'm nervous, it's the whole room.
*{sfx:Hum}The whole room flickers.*
...Like that. Sorry.
It's a small fire! It's a starter fire! Fires have gotta start somewhere!
*{sfx:Sizzle}He stomps on it. It goes out. Mostly.*
Sorry. That one's on me. Most things are a bit on me.
You: Okay. What ARE you, exactly?
Ah. Good question. Big question. Honestly? Not a hundred percent sure.
I've been in these walls a long time. Long enough to come up with a few [theories]. Main one: I'm a surge. Or a really committed static charge.
Sorry. You asked a small question and I've given you a big answer. I do that.

choices.text: A surge with an Australian accent?
Whatever you are, you're cute.
Can you be a surge somewhere else? I'm on a schedule.

lines: You: How many theories?
Forty-one. Theory one: surge. Theory nine: committed static charge. Theory thirty: I'm the millennium bug, and I owe everyone an apology.
Theory forty-one is just a drawing of a sad lightbulb. I was having a week.
Have I got an accent? Huh. Imported components, maybe. Heaps of fittings are made overseas.
*He looks briefly worried.*
...Never met a fuse box with a passport, though.
*Every bulb in the room goes up a notch. Then another. {sfx:Spark}One pops.*
Cute. Right. Yep. Thank you. That's... thanks.
Sorry about the bulb. You'll need a new bulb. Sorry.
Oh! Course. Yep. Sorry. I'll just...
*He shrinks back toward the fuse box, then stops.*
...Can I ask what the schedule is? Not being nosy. They're my walls. Sort of. If that's... alright?
You: Thirty days. I fix this house for real, or the city knocks it down. On day thirty, an [inspector|dan] goes through every room.
You: And an electrician quoted me forty grand for a full rewire. I have eleven. So I'm doing the minimum to scrape past.
*{sfx:Hum}The lamp browns out, long and slow, like a sigh.*
The minimum! Right! Love the minimum. Very... efficient.

choices.text: You don't sound sure. What do you actually think?
Great. Then you can help me cut corners.
Glad you're on board. You can be my assistant.

lines: You: Inspector Dan. From the council. Windbreaker, moustache, clipboard.
A clipboard. Right. Lovely. I'm sure he's lovely.
Does he look behind the faceplates? Not that... I'm just asking. For a friend.
*He pushes his glasses up.*
The friend is the wiring.
*He stares at you like nobody has ever asked him that. Possibly nobody has.*
What do I... oh. Um. Well. Technically, a house this old, with what's in these walls, the minimum's a bit... It's a bit of a fire...
It's fine! It's your house. Your call. Sorry. Forget I said anything.
*Wyatt will remember that you asked.*
Corners. Yep. Love a corner. Cutting 'em.
*{sfx:Sizzle}Somewhere inside the wall, something goes tsssss.*
...That's just a wall noise. Ignore the wall. I do.
*{sfx:Hum}He lights up. Actually lights up. There's a glow.*
Assistant! Yeah! I can assist! I'm basically an apprentice. To... someone. Somewhere.
Just tell me what to do. I'm really good at being told what to do.
*He swings the fuse box door open like he's showing you round his flat. Every switch inside is labeled in faded marker: KITCHEN?, LOUNGE (PROBABLY), DON'T, and one that just says [MYSTERY|mystery].*
This is me. Home sweet home. Sorry about the labels. They're not mine. Someone with very confident handwriting and no idea what he was doing.
*He pushes his glasses up his nose. {sfx:Zap}A spark jumps off the copper rim. He yelps at himself.*
Sorry. Static. Happens every time I'm nervous. Which is every time.

choices.text: Your glasses keep sparking. It's very cute.
Who writes DON'T on a fuse box?
So you live in a cupboard. Cool.

lines: You: What does MYSTERY do?
Nobody knows. I flicked it once. Somewhere in the house, a doorbell rang.
*He lowers his voice.*
We haven't got a doorbell. I've been looking for it ever since.
*{sfx:Hum}Every bulb in the room starts blinking. It could be Morse code. It's probably spelling HELP.*
*His glasses fog over completely. He doesn't take them off. He just stands there, blind and glowing.*
I'm not flustered! This is just my resting frequency.
No idea. Same bloke as the other labels. But look, it's underlined three times. He meant that one.
*He gazes at it with something like respect.*
I've never flicked it. It's the only instruction in this house anyone's ever followed.
It's a box. A fuse box. It's very different.
*He looks hurt for half a second. Then he nods.*
...Fair. But it's my box.
*{sfx:Hum}Something by the stairs hums. It's your new dehumidifier: a plain white box with a water tank and a little green light.*
Sorry. Last thing. That dehumidifier. It's plugged into the socket by the stairs, and that socket's a bit...
I can feel it from here. Like a loose tooth.
Could you maybe move it? Not that it's my business. It's a bit my business.

choices.text: I'll move it. Thanks for telling me.
You're worried about a dehumidifier?
It stays where it is.

lines: *You move the dehumidifier to the socket by the window. The lamp breathes out. So does Wyatt.*
Thanks. Honestly. Most people don't move things just cause I said.
Not the dehumidifier. The socket. Those things pull current all night, and that socket's down to one screw, hanging on for dear life.
One very tired screw, doing the job of four, and nobody's ever said thanks.
...I relate to the screw.
No worries! Totally fine. It'll be...
*{sfx:Sizzle}The socket by the stairs crackles faintly.*
...Fine. Probably fine.
*It's getting dark. You both reach for the lamp switch at the same moment. Your fingertips meet.*
*{sfx:Zap}ZAP.*
Sorry! Sorry. That's a thing my body does. When someone's nice to me.
*Your hair is standing on end. So is his. His glasses have slid right down to the tip of his nose. You both look like dandelions.*
It was really nice meeting you, {player}. Can I call you {player}? Is that... alright? Great. Sorry. Bye.
*He folds himself back into the fuse box. The door shuts. Then, very quietly, it opens again.*
Bye.
You asked what I thought. Last week. About the wiring.
I've been thinking about that. A lot. A LOT a lot. Anyway! Hi.
Oh! {player}. Hi. Not upset about last week. I don't really get upset. I get... slightly dimmer.
*He is slightly dimmer.*

*Wyatt is sitting cross-legged by the fuse box, hopelessly tangled in an extension cord, humming [a song|song]. His glasses are hanging off one ear. Folded on top of the fuse box, very neatly, is a pink [towel].*
{player}! Hi! Sorry. One sec. I'm in a knot. I was checking all the cords in the house, and one of them checked me back.

choices.text: Here, let me help you untangle.
Checking the cords for what?
You look ridiculous.

lines: You: What's the song?
Dunno! It's always in my head. Something about partying like it's a certain year.
*{sfx:Hum}Every bulb in the room dips at the word 'year.'*
Big year, whatever it was. Everyone was gonna party. I reckon I missed it.
You: Whose towel?
Oh! Tyler's. He wants it 'folded in thirds, Private. Like a flag.' He's a tile. He doesn't technically use towels. He likes knowing it's there.
*The lamp flickers twice. Wyatt studies the extension cord with enormous concentration.*
He's just used to people saying yes. And I'm really good at yes. Anyway!
*You start unwinding the cord. Your hands brush. {sfx:Zap}Somewhere, something goes bzzt.*
Sorry! Sorry. That was me. You're very... [grounding]. Did you know that?
You: Grounding?
Like a third prong. Like a copper rod in wet soil.
That's the most romantic thing I know how to say. Sorry. It's a lot.
Every cord in this house is somebody's bad idea. I can feel them all, like stones in a shoe.
*He holds up the end he's tangled in. It's been taped to itself in three places.*
See? Someone fixed this by making it worse. Very confidently. Same handwriting as the fuse box.
Yeah. Fair.
*He tries to push his glasses up. His hand is tied to his ankle. He nudges them up with his shoulder instead.*
...Nobody looks dignified in a knot. I'm doing my best.
*You show him the plan: a box of shiny new circuit breakers, thirty amps each, and a paint chart called [Greige Expectations|greige].*
You: The breakers keep tripping, so I'm swapping the fifteens for thirties. No more tripping. New faceplates, a feature wall, and it all looks perfect for Dan on day thirty.
*{sfx:Hum}Wyatt looks at the thirty-amp breakers. Every light in the room starts to flicker. Fast.*
Yeah! No! I mean, yeah. Great. No worries. If that's what you... yeah.
*The flickering is now very fast. It's basically a disco.*

choices.text: Wyatt. The lights. What aren't you telling me?
Great! Hand me the screwdriver, assistant.
You'd tell me if something was wrong, right?

lines: You: It's a very popular gray.
It's gray AND beige. It's a color that's too scared to commit to being a color.
...I relate to it, actually. Lovely choice. Sorry.
Course! Absolutely. Straight away.
*{sfx:Spark}A bulb pops.*
...Mostly straight away. Eventually. Within the week.

choices.text: Wyatt.
Okay. Then we're good.

lines: *He opens his mouth. Closes it. Opens it again.*
It's just... a breaker's meant to trip before the wire gets hot. That's its whole job. It's a smoke alarm for the wire.
Put a thirty on fifteen-amp wire and it never trips. The wire just gets hotter and hotter inside the wall where nobody can see, and then one night, when it's cold and every heater's on...
*He catches himself.*
Sorry! Sorry. That was a lot of words. I went fast. I do that. It's your call. Honestly. Ignore me.

choices.text: Don't apologize. That's the most useful thing anyone's said to me all week.
Is there a way to do it properly AND cheaply?
Noted. But I can't afford new wire, so the thirties go in.

lines: *Every light in the house steadies. Warm. Bright. For the first time since you moved in, nothing flickers.*
...Oh. You're not cross?
Nobody's ever not cross. Gary was always...
*He stops.*
I don't know a Gary. Who's Gary?
Properly and cheaply? They don't really get along. They're like water and a toaster.
But I know which circuits are the worst. We could do those first, properly, and save the rest for later. If that's... alright?
*You do the two worst circuits together. He talks you through every wire, apologizes for talking, then keeps talking.*
*You put the thirties in. Wyatt hands you each one like he's handing you a live grenade. Very politely.*
{sfx:SwitchOn}There you go. All in. No more tripping. Brilliant. Great job.
*The wall behind the fuse box is very slightly warm. Neither of you mentions it.*
*Afterwards you sit on the floor by the fuse box with a packet of biscuits. You eat. He holds one, very politely, the way you'd hold someone else's baby.*
*His glasses have slid down his nose again. He pushes them up with one cable-braided knuckle. {sfx:Zap}A spark jumps off the copper rim.*
Sorry. Static. Every time I push them up. Which is every time I'm nervous. Which is... now. Mostly now.

choices.text: You're the most alive thing in this house, you know.
Here. Let me clean those for you.
Can you not spark on my new floor?

lines: Alive. Ha! Yeah. Alive. Totally.
*A long, thoughtful flicker.*
...Theory fourteen is that I'm a really long-life light bulb. Those go for decades. Nobody remembers putting them in.
*You slide his glasses off, breathe on the lenses and polish them on your sleeve. He goes the color of a heating element.*
*Without them, he squints at you like you're a very lovely blur.*
You're still really nice-looking at this resolution. Sorry. Can I have them back? I'd like the high-definition version.
Sorry. Yep. On it.
*He tucks his hands under his arms. {sfx:Spark}Sparks come out of his elbows instead.*
...Working on it.
So. Um. How's your week been? Not the house. You. Sorry. Is that a weird question? I don't get out of the wall much.

choices.text: Honestly? Things are getting a bit flirty around the house.
Long. Where are you from, anyway? You sound like a holiday.
Busy. I should get back to it.
Why are you being weird?

lines: Oh! Great! That's great. That's fine. Totally fine.
*{sfx:Hum}The lamp browns out, long and slow, like a sigh.*
That's a lamp thing. Old lamp. It's fine.

choices.text: Wyatt, the lamp doesn't think it's fine.
Good. Glad you're cool with it.

lines: The lamp's very dramatic. It doesn't speak for me.
*The lamp flickers indignantly.*
...It speaks a little bit for me.
So cool. Coolest. I'm basically a fridge.
*{sfx:Sizzle}From somewhere deep in the wall comes a tiny electrical whimper.*
A holiday! Ha. I reckon I sound like a sparky. That's what you call an electrician, where I'm from. 'Get a sparky in.'
*He frowns.*
...Where am I from? Fuse boxes aren't from places. Huh.
Oh! Course. Yep. Go. Houses don't fix themselves.
*He glances at the fuse box, then back at you, and pushes his glasses up.*
...Well. One of them's trying.
I'm not being weird! I'm being sociable. I read about it in a magazine someone left in the wall.
It's from 1998, so some of the advice might be a bit off. It says to ask about your pager.
*He walks you to the living room door. Well, he flickers along the light switches beside you.*
Thanks for today, {player}. Come back next week? If that's... yeah. Come back.
*Before you can say a word, Wyatt holds up both hands.*
Before you say anything. The blackout. During Lukey's candle dinner. Wasn't me.
*A long pause.*
{sfx:PowerDown}...It was me. It was completely me. He was doing a lovely candle thing, and I got a... feeling, and the whole house went.
Lukey says it's fine. He said it in a very damp voice.
*The wall behind the fuse box is warm. Properly warm. There's a smell like [toast], and nobody is making toast.*
*{sfx:Spark}Wyatt is pacing. Little sparks follow his feet like nervous puppies. His glasses keep fogging up from the heat.*
Hi! Hi, {player}. Don't panic. Everything's fine. The wall's just having a warm week.

choices.text: It's the thirty-amp breakers, isn't it?
Wyatt. Is my house going to catch fire?
Dan's never going to open a wall. Leave it.

lines: You: Why does my wall smell like toast?
That's the old rubber on the wires. It smells like toast when it cooks. Fun fact!
...Horrible fact. Sorry. Horrible fun fact.
*He stops pacing.*
...Yeah. It is. Them, and the old wiring behind them.
It's not a warm week. It's a warning. Sorry. I should've said it louder. I said it a bit. I should've said it a lot.
*He opens his mouth to say 'no worries.' Nothing comes out. He tries again.*
...Yeah. Probably. Not today. But one night, when it's cold and every heater's on.
That's the first time I've said that out loud. It felt horrible. Bit good, though?
Right. Yep. Leave it. He won't open a wall. Nobody will. Till one night, when it opens itself.
*{sfx:Sizzle}The toast smell gets stronger.*
...Sorry. Could you just touch the wall? Just touch it. Then decide.
*You touch it. It's the temperature of a cup of tea.*
You: ...Okay. Get me a crowbar.
*You pull the drywall off. Wyatt holds the flashlight. Well, he IS the flashlight. He glows a bit brighter, on purpose.*
*Inside: wires spliced with sticky tape, a fossilized ham sandwich, a cable that just stops, and a yellowed newspaper stuffed into a gap as insulation.*
Ha. Newspaper. That's not insulation, Gary.
*He freezes.*
...Who's Gary?
*You unfold it. The Heartbreak Lane Herald, January 2nd, 2000. The headline: 'Y2K: NO CASUALTIES.'*

*Underneath, in very small print: 'Australian apprentice electrician Wyatt Doyle, 26, of Wollongong, died in a New Year's Eve wiring accident on Heartbreak Lane. He was in the country on a working holiday.'*
*{sfx:PowerDown}Every light in the house goes out. Then, very slowly, the lamp comes back on.*
No casualties. And then me. Underneath. In the little writing.
They put me under the bug.

choices.text: Take his hand.
Wyatt. You were a person. A whole person.
Wollongong? Is that a real place?
So you're a ghost. Does this affect the budget?

lines: *{sfx:Zap}ZAP. You don't let go.*
*{sfx:Hum}The zap turns into a hum. Warm and steady, like a fridge at night.*
...You're still holding on.
Nobody holds on. With electricity, you let go. That's the rule.
A person. With a birthday. And a... and a mum.
*He takes his glasses off and wipes them on his shirt for much longer than glasses need.*
She rang every Sunday. Reverse charges. I'd forgotten that.
...Do you know what an international call cost in 1999? Bloody hell, Mum.
It's real! It's south of Sydney! There's a beach and a lighthouse and a really good chicken shop!
*He stops.*
I remember the chicken shop. {player}. I remember the CHICKEN SHOP.
*It is the happiest you have ever seen anyone find out they're dead.*
*The lamp dims.*
...Probably. Sorry. I'll try to be a cheaper ghost.
*{sfx:Sizzle}He tries to laugh. It comes out as a small fizz.*
It's coming back. New Year's Eve. A bloke called Mr. Kowalski lived here. Thought the millennium bug would turn his toaster against him. Four hundred tins of beans and a generator.
He paid my boss, Gary, to wire the generator straight into the house. No switch. Gary said it'd be fine. Gary said everything'd be fine. Gary once said that about a ladder.
I knew it was wrong. Knew it the way you know a song's out of tune. And I didn't say anything. Didn't want to be a [bother].
At midnight, Mr. Kowalski flicked every switch in the house to 'confuse the bug.' And I was holding the bit Gary said would be fine.
*A small, embarrassed flicker.*
So. Y2K was real. It just only happened to me.

choices.text: You knew it was wrong. You still know. So tell me.
And now I'm asking you to patch it. Exactly like Gary.
That's a great story. I still can't afford a rewire.

lines: You: You'd never be a bother.
I was twenty-six and four weeks off the plane. Everything felt like a bother. Ordering a coffee felt like a bother.
I said sorry to a vending machine once. It hadn't even given me the chips yet.
*He takes a breath. Every light in the house takes one with him.*
*He looks at you for a long time.*
...A bit. Yeah. Sorry. I mean... no. Not sorry. Yeah.
*The lamp browns out. Then it comes back on brighter, like it's decided something.*
Don't patch it. Please. Rewire it. Properly. New copper, the right breakers, the lot.
I know it's forty grand. I know you've got eleven. I'll help you find every cheap way that isn't dangerous. There's heaps. I know all of them.
I just don't want it to happen to anyone else. Not to you. Especially not to you.
*He's shaking a little. Every bulb in the house is perfectly steady.*
...That's what I think. Sorry for the... no. That's what I think.

choices.text: Okay. We do it properly. Thank you for telling me.
Kiss him.
I'll think about it.

lines: *{sfx:PowerUp}Every light in the house comes on at once. Even the ones that aren't plugged in.*
Properly? Like, properly properly? Copper?
You: Copper.
*He makes the noise a kettle makes right before it clicks off.*
*{sfx:Kiss}You kiss him. It's soft and tingly, like licking a nine-volt battery, but in a good way.*
*{sfx:Spark}Somewhere down the street, three streetlights pop. When you pull back, his glasses have fogged solid. He leaves them. He's smiling too hard to deal with it.*
You: That's for saying it. And yes. We'll do it properly.
...I'm going to say things way more often.
Yeah. Course. No worries.
*He means it about sixty percent.*
...Think hard, though? Please?
*You spend the afternoon pulling Gary's cable out of the wall together. He talks you through every splice, fast and nerdy, then catches himself every single time.*
Sorry. I'm doing the thing. The fast thing.
Can I ask you something? It's not about cable.

choices.text: Ask me anything.
Go on. I've got a crowbar and all afternoon.

lines: *He winds a loop of Gary's old cable round his elbow, very carefully, not looking at you.*
*He pushes his glasses up. Then again, although they haven't moved.*
Who do you like? In the house. Sorry! For the wiring. I need to know which circuits to prioritize.

choices.text: Honestly? I've got a bit of a thing going with some of the others.
You. Prioritize your own circuit.
All of you. You're my favorite weirdos.
That's none of your business, Wyatt.

lines: That's fine! That's great. They're great. Fine.
*The lamp browns out. {sfx:Spark}Out in the hall, a bulb quietly pops.*
...It's fine.

choices.text: It's okay to not be fine, you know.
Good.

lines: Is it?
*He actually thinks about it.*
...Ask me again next week. I'm working up to it. One 'no' at a time.
*Every streetlight on Heartbreak Lane brightens. Two streets over, a car alarm goes off from sheer excitement.*
Me. Right. Okay. Prioritizing... me. My circuit. First.
...I'm going to need a minute.
Favorite weirdos! I'm somebody's favorite weirdo!
*He writes it on the inside of the fuse box door, under DON'T, in very neat capitals.*
Yeah. No. You're right. Sorry.
*He dims. Then, slowly, he brightens again.*
Actually, no. It's a bit my business. They're my walls. I hear everything. You sing to the kettle. It's very flat.
*{sfx:RadioStatic}The radio on the mantelpiece crackles into an emergency bulletin: 'BIG STORM SATURDAY. Heavy rain, high winds, power cuts across the county.'*
Power cuts. Right. Everyone'll get their generators out.
*He goes very still.*
People do silly things with generators.

choices.text: Then we'll do it right. You'll make sure of it.
Relax. Mrs. Pruitt next door is lending me hers.
You're scared of a bit of rain?

lines: Me. Making sure.
*He tries the idea on, like a jacket.*
...Yeah. I can do that. I think. I'd like to.
Mrs. Pruitt's generator? The one with the crossbow sticker?
...How are you planning to plug it in?
You: Into the house?
*Every light in the house turns slowly to look at you.*
Let's talk about that. Please.
Not the rain. What people do in it.
*Sulky flicker.*
*Late. The wall's still open. The newspaper is propped on the mantelpiece like a diploma.*
Twenty-seven years working out what I am. Forty-one theories. And I'm just a bloke who didn't say something.
Next time, I'm going to say something. I promise.
Night, {player}.
*{sfx:Thunder}{sfx:Rain}Saturday. The storm hits Heartbreak Lane like it's holding a grudge. The rain is going sideways. The power's been out since breakfast.*
*The only light in the living room is Wyatt.*
{player}. Love. Sorry, that slipped out. No. It didn't slip. Love.
*It's the first time he's called you that. He has clearly been practicing on the toaster.*
*{sfx:Thunder}{sfx:Rain}Saturday. The storm hits Heartbreak Lane like it's holding a grudge. The rain is going sideways. The power's been out since breakfast.*
*The only light in the living room is Wyatt.*
{player}! You're here. Good. Bad. Good that you're here. Bad everything else.
*{sfx:WaterSplash}Water is coming in under the back door. The sump pump needs power, or the basement floods, then the kitchen.*
*The fridge is dark. The dehumidifier is dark. The brightest things in the room are Wyatt's glasses: two little copper circles, glowing.*
*You've borrowed [Mrs. Pruitt's|pruitt] generator. And from the junk drawer, an old orange cord with a plug on both ends. Someone has written GARY on it in marker.*
*Wyatt sees the cord. Every light that was already off somehow goes more off.*
That's... ha. That's Gary's.
*{sfx:Thunder}You head for the dryer socket. Plug that in, and the generator feeds straight back into the house. No switch. Exactly like New Year's Eve, 1999.*
It's... it might be... if that's what you... if that's...

choices.text: Wyatt. Say it.
What would you do?
No time! The pump needs power. I'm plugging it in.

lines: You: She said I can keep it as long as I bring it back full and ask no questions.
...I've got questions.
Why does a generator need a crossbow sticker?
*He looks at you. You look back. You wait. You don't fill the silence for him. It's the hardest thing you've done all month.*
What would I...
*For one second he looks twenty-six and four weeks off the plane.*
*You reach for the socket. The plug is an inch away.*
{sfx:Zap}NO.

*{sfx:PowerUp}Every light in the house blazes on at once. There's no power. There's no reason. The whole of 12 Heartbreak Lane is lit up like a stadium, and Wyatt is standing in the middle of it, very solid.*
No. Don't plug that in. Sorry. No. Not sorry. NO.

That cord backfeeds the panel. No [transfer switch|switch], Gary's old splices, the lot. It sends power out to the street, so the bloke up the pole fixing the lines gets all of it. And the house goes up like a Christmas tree. With you in it.
I didn't say it in 1999. I'm saying it now. Put Gary's cord down.

choices.text: Put the cord down. 'You were right. Thank you.'
Okay! Okay. Bossy. I like it.
Don't you dare shout at me.

lines: You: What's a transfer switch?
It's a switch that means the house runs on the street OR the generator, never both. It takes turns. It's a very polite switch.
I love it. I'd marry it. Sorry. Not the time.
*You put the cord down. He stares at it. Then at you.*
You listened. I said a thing, and you listened.
Okay. Okay! Then let's do it properly. Fast.
*He goes pink. The stadium lighting goes a bit pinker too. His glasses fog.*
I'm not bossy. I'm... yeah, okay, I'm being a bit bossy. It's going really well, actually.
*He flinches. Then he doesn't apologize. You can see how much that costs him.*
I'm not shouting at you. I'm shouting at the cord.
...Bit at you. Put it down. Please. But put it down.
*So you do it his way. He talks, you work.*
*Gary's last splice comes out. The right breaker goes in. The pump gets its own lead, straight to the generator, outside, exactly like it says on the generator in very large letters.*
*{sfx:PowerUp}The generator roars. The pump kicks in. The water stops rising. By the window, the dehumidifier's green light blinks back on, on its good socket.*

*{sfx:FixComplete}For the first time in twenty-seven years, the wiring in 12 Heartbreak Lane is exactly what it should be. You'll be paying off the copper until you're forty. You find you don't mind.*
*Wyatt's stadium glow settles into something soft and steady. No buzz. No flicker.*
...Oh. It's so quiet. Is this what a normal house sounds like? It's so QUIET.
*He holds his hands up to the lamp. The braided cable of his forearms is quiet. The thin wire veins along his jaw have stopped glowing. Nothing crackles.*
Look. I'm not humming. I always hum. Twenty-seven years of humming, and it's just... stopped.
Is this what calm feels like? It's weird. I hate it. I love it. Mostly love it.

choices.text: Dan's going to love this on day thirty.
Calm looks good on you.

lines: Dan! The inspection! Will he look behind the... yes. He'll look behind everything. That's his whole job.
*His glasses fog. Then, slowly, they clear.*
...Let him. Let him open every faceplate in the house. It's right. I've never been able to say that about a wall before.
Yeah?
*He pushes his glasses up. No spark. He stares at his own finger like it's betrayed him.*
I don't know what to do with my hands now. I used to spark. Now I just... have hands.
*He sits on the arm of the sofa: steady, solid, not sparking at all. He looks a bit stunned.*
I said no. To you. And you're still here. And so's the house.
I said no to Tyler too. He ordered me to keep the bathroom fan going through the storm. I said no. He called me 'insubordinate.'
*One small flicker, for old times' sake.*
He's never called me anything but Private before.
...Can I say another thing? While I've got the hang of it?

choices.text: Go on. Say anything.
Is this about me and the others? Say it.

lines: You've been the best thing in this house since about five minutes after I fell out of the fuse box. I'm mad about you.
You don't have to feel the same. I just didn't want to be twenty-seven years late again.
*No flicker. Not one. Just him, saying it.*
Yeah. It is.
It's not fine. I said it was fine. The lamp knew. The lamp's always known.
I'm a one-person bloke. Always have been. I'd want to be your one person. If that's... no. No 'if that's alright.' That's what I want.
You don't have to give it to me. But now you know.

choices.text: Now I know.
And the blackout at Lukey's dinner?

lines: Yeah. That was me. Here's the bit I didn't say.
I was jealous. He was lighting candles for you, and I got a feeling, and the feeling took out the whole house.
Sorry about the dinner. Not sorry about the feeling.
*{sfx:Rain}The storm is easing. Rain ticks on the window. Wyatt is glowing faintly at the edges, the way people do when they're finally finished with something.*
Well. That's two things I've said. I reckon that might've been it. The thing I was stuck on.

choices.text: I'm so proud of you.
Keep going. Say all of it. To me.
Only took you twenty-seven years.

lines: *He goes very pink, very steadily. Not a flicker.*
Proud. Of me. Okay. I'm keeping that one in the walls forever.
*He laughs. A real one, no fizz.*
You've got a gorgeous smile. Your drill technique's dodgy. And I'm keeping the good torch. That's three. I'm on a roll.
Twenty-seven years and one bloody good flipper.
*He grins.*
Yeah, nah. Fair.
*The next morning, the storm has passed. Wyatt flicks the lamp on and off, just because he can. {sfx:SwitchOn}Nothing flickers. Nothing sparks. Nothing apologizes.*
So. The wiring's right. I said the thing. I reckon I get to choose now. Stay, or go wherever surges go. Probably Wollongong.
I know what I want. I'd just like to hear what you want first. That's not me asking permission. That's manners.

choices.text: Stay. With me. I love you, Wyatt.
Stay. With me.
I love you. Go home. Go find your chicken shop.
Go. You've earned it.
That's up to you, Wyatt.
That's up to you, Wyatt.

lines: *{sfx:Kiss}He kisses you. No zap. Just warm. His glasses end up somewhere in your hair. Neither of you goes looking.*
I'm staying. I want to. That's me wanting something, out loud.
Also I've got forty-one theories to cross off, and I'd like to do it with you.

v4_rs2.fxText: The lights went out. On purpose, this time.
lines: *Much later.*
...Best power cut of my life.
*He takes your hands. Warm. Steady. No zap.*
I love you. I do. And I've only just learned how to say no, so I'm going to use it on the hardest one first.
No. I'm not staying. You'd have me patching things for you forever, and I'd let you. I'd say yes every time.
*He kisses your forehead.*
Yeah, nah. Look after the wiring, {player}. I'll know if you don't.
*The lights glow gold, then soft, and then he's gone. The porch light flickers twice.*
*He searches your face. Then he nods, slowly.*
Yeah. You're right. You always know what the wiring needs.
I love you too. Said it first go. Did you notice? No 'if that's alright.'
*{sfx:Kiss}He kisses you once, warm, no zap. The lights glow gold, then soft, and then he's gone. The porch light flickers twice.*
*He grins and gives you a very Australian thumbs up.*
Best mate I've ever had, alive or... whatever this was.
Keep the dehumidifier off the stairs socket, yeah? Fix that screw. And tell the toaster I forgive it.
*He goes out in a warm, steady glow. No spark. No flicker. Gone, the way a light goes when someone switches it off properly.*
Up to me.
*He sits with that for a long moment.*
Nobody's ever... yeah. Thanks.
Then I'll go. Not because I want to leave. Because I can. Because I said the thing.
No worries, {player}. And for once I actually mean it.
*A soft, steady glow. Then nothing. The porch light flickers twice, just to say bye.*
Up to me? Okay. Then I'll go.
I'm not staying for someone who only asks what I think when the house is on fire.
*He says it gently. He doesn't say sorry. He has never been prouder of himself.*
*He's gone before you can answer. Taped to the fuse box is a note in very neat capitals: NO WORRIES. (SOME WORRIES.) -W*
We've had our chat today, {player}. I'm a fuse box, not talkback radio.
Come back next week? If that's... yeah. Please. I'll be here. I'm always here. That's sort of the problem.
Hey, love. I told the kettle it boils too loud. Out loud. To its face.
*He pushes his glasses up. He looks thrilled and terrified in exactly equal measure.*
It didn't say anything back. I reckon I won.
*The porch light flickers twice when you come home. Then it holds steady, like it's being brave about it.*
*The lights are steady and quiet. Inside the fuse box, every switch has a new label in very neat capitals. The one that used to say DON'T now says DONE.*
*The note's still taped to the fuse box: NO WORRIES. (SOME WORRIES.) -W. Underneath, in smaller capitals: THE STAIRS SOCKET IS STILL DODGY. You move the dehumidifier anyway.*
